Woman with long dark wavy hair and face-framing layers that fall past the chin to the collarbones, smiling softly in a three-quarter portrait near a window

Flat-lay on a light wooden surface of a handwritten salon note reading 'length: just below jaw, layers start: below chin, fringe: curtain, cheekbone length, part: middle or side', beside a black comb, cutting shears and two printed photos of wavy brown bob haircuts shown from behind, with a potted plant in the corner.

issues: Bangs and fringe: The article attributes the claim that a middle part helps elongate a round face to Davines, but a later section cites the same source for something different. More importantly, the Revlon URL slug is 'how-to-style-wavy-natural-hair-2', so it may not be a round-face source. The quoted evidence matches the claim, so this is only a minor concern.

Where Stylists Disagree: The article says the 36-cut roundup 'recommends a choppy lob with blunt ends and a sleek, blunt lob' while 'tell[ing] readers to avoid blunt bobs'. The evidence supports this, so this is not an error.

Short Cuts and Pixies: The article states 'pixie with a deep side part and long bangs' is a suggestion from the site. The evidence is truncated at 'deep s...', so 'side part' is an unverified completion of the text.

issues: Image 2 failed validation: Image failed editorial review: ["The two heads show essentially identical hair; the face-framing layers do not visibly differ, so the diagram fails to demonstrate the contrast between layers starting at the cheekbones and layers starting below the chin.","The left arrow is a long curved line that points to the cheek/face area rather than clearly marking where a shortest layer begins, which is misleading about the 'starts at cheekbones' concept.","The right arrow points to hair near the jaw/neck, but the hair there shows no distinct shortest layer, so the 'starts below chin' marker does not correspond to any visible feature.","The head is not clearly a round-face example and the illustration is more detailed painterly shading than the requested simple line art, reducing clarity as an educational diagram."]
